# Dataset schema cheatsheet (auto-generated by scripts/schema_cheatsheet.py)

SQLite dialect. Dates are ISO TEXT. Full details: src/data/datasets.json


## ecommerce

- **customers** (4520 rows): customer_id:INTEGER, full_name:TEXT, email:TEXT, phone:TEXT, gender:TEXT, city:TEXT, state:TEXT, signup_date:DATE, signup_date_raw:TEXT, acquisition_channel:TEXT, is_prime:INTEGER
- **products** (420 rows): product_id:INTEGER, sku:TEXT, product_name:TEXT, category:TEXT, sub_category:TEXT, brand:TEXT, mrp:REAL, cost_price:REAL, is_active:INTEGER
- **orders** (10100 rows): order_id:INTEGER, customer_id:INTEGER, order_date:DATE, order_time:TEXT, order_status:TEXT, sales_channel:TEXT, coupon_code:TEXT, discount_amount:REAL, shipping_fee:REAL, total_amount:REAL, delivery_date:DATE
- **order_items** (20157 rows): order_item_id:INTEGER, order_id:INTEGER, product_id:INTEGER, quantity:INTEGER, unit_price:REAL, discount_pct:INTEGER, line_total:REAL
- **payments** (10399 rows): payment_id:INTEGER, order_id:INTEGER, payment_method:TEXT, amount:REAL, payment_status:TEXT, payment_date:DATE, transaction_ref:TEXT
- **returns** (1909 rows): return_id:INTEGER, order_item_id:INTEGER, order_id:INTEGER, return_date:DATE, return_reason:TEXT, return_status:TEXT, refund_amount:REAL
- FKs: orders.customer_id->customers.customer_id; order_items.order_id->orders.order_id; order_items.product_id->products.product_id; payments.order_id->orders.order_id; returns.order_item_id->order_items.order_item_id; returns.order_id->orders.order_id
- Quality issues: orders: ~1% of rows (about 100) are exact duplicates (same order_id repeated); so orders.order_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint. | customers: 20 exact duplicate customer rows; customers.customer_id is therefore not unique. | customers.email is NULL for ~8% of rows, phone ~3%, gender ~4%, city ~3% (state is NULL whenever city is NULL). | customers.city: ~10% of values have inconsistent casing or stray whitespace ('mumbai', ' Mumbai', 'DELHI '). | customers.signup_date_raw: free-text dates in four formats (YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, '5 Mar 2023', 'Mar 5, 2023') and ~3% NULL; signup_date holds the clean value. | products.category: ~2% of values have inconsistent casing or whitespace. | order_items.unit_price: 12 rows are 100x too high (entry errors) which inflates order totals for those orders. | CSV only - orders.order_date: ~18% of rows are written as DD-MM-YYYY instead of YYYY-MM-DD. | CSV only - orders.total_amount: ~12% of rows are text like '₹1,234.50' (symbol and thousands commas). | CSV only - returns.refund_amount: ~50% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian digit grouping (e.g. '₹1,23,456.00'). | payments: ~5% of online-paid orders have an extra earlier 'Failed' attempt row, so order_id is not unique in payments.
- Signals (instructor notes): [Instructor note] Festive spikes: order volume rises ~1.5-1.9x in the Diwali windows (Oct 8-16 2023, Nov 6-14 2023, Sep 27-Oct 6 2024, Oct 24-Nov 3 2024); weekends are ~18% higher; steady growth through 2024. | [Instructor note] Fashion and Footwear have return rates of ~21% and ~15% (mostly 'Size / fit issue'), versus ~1% for Grocery. | [Instructor note] COD orders are cancelled ~11% of the time and RTO another ~7%, versus ~3.5% cancellation for prepaid. | [Instructor note] Tier-2 cities use COD far more (~34% vs ~18%) and have longer delivery times. | [Instructor note] Prime members (22% of customers) place roughly twice the orders; customer activity is heavy-tailed (a minority of customers drive most orders). | [Instructor note] Data-entry outliers (12 order_items with 100x unit_price) distort average order value unless handled.

## food_delivery

- **restaurants** (600 rows): restaurant_id:INTEGER, restaurant_name:TEXT, cuisine:TEXT, city:TEXT, price_band:TEXT, avg_prep_minutes:INTEGER, is_cloud_kitchen:INTEGER, onboarded_date:DATE
- **delivery_partners** (908 rows): partner_id:INTEGER, partner_name:TEXT, city:TEXT, vehicle_type:TEXT, joined_date:DATE, phone:TEXT, is_active:INTEGER
- **deliveries** (15120 rows): delivery_id:INTEGER, restaurant_id:INTEGER, partner_id:INTEGER, customer_id:INTEGER, city:TEXT, order_date:DATE, order_time:DATETIME, delivered_time:DATETIME, distance_km:REAL, promised_minutes:INTEGER, actual_minutes:INTEGER, delay_minutes:INTEGER, order_value:REAL, delivery_fee:REAL, payment_mode:TEXT, weather:TEXT, delivery_status:TEXT, cancel_reason:TEXT
- **ratings** (8630 rows): rating_id:INTEGER, delivery_id:INTEGER, restaurant_id:INTEGER, partner_id:INTEGER, food_rating:INTEGER, delivery_rating:INTEGER, overall_rating:INTEGER, review_text:TEXT, rated_at:DATETIME
- **promo_usage** (5474 rows): usage_id:INTEGER, delivery_id:INTEGER, promo_code:TEXT, discount_amount:REAL, is_new_user:INTEGER, used_at:DATETIME
- FKs: deliveries.restaurant_id->restaurants.restaurant_id; deliveries.partner_id->delivery_partners.partner_id; ratings.delivery_id->deliveries.delivery_id; ratings.restaurant_id->restaurants.restaurant_id; ratings.partner_id->delivery_partners.partner_id; promo_usage.delivery_id->deliveries.delivery_id
- Quality issues: deliveries: ~0.8% of rows (about 120) are exact duplicates by delivery_id, so delivery_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint. | delivery_partners: 8 exact duplicate partner rows. | deliveries.actual_minutes, delay_minutes, delivered_time and cancel_reason are NULL by design for cancelled orders (~5-6% of rows). | deliveries.order_value: 8 rows are 100x outliers (e.g. 41,200 instead of 412). | restaurants.city ~8% and delivery_partners.city ~6% (and deliveries.city ~3%) have inconsistent casing or whitespace; restaurants.city ~2% NULL; delivery_partners.phone ~5% NULL. | promo_usage.promo_code: ~4% of values have inconsistent casing/whitespace. | CSV only - deliveries.order_time: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS instead of ISO. | CSV only - deliveries.order_value: ~15% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping (e.g. '₹1,250'). | CSV only - ratings.rated_at: ~25% of rows in DD-MM-YYYY format. | CSV only - promo_usage.discount_amount: ~20% of rows are text like '₹75.00'.
- Signals (instructor notes): [Instructor note] Delivery delay drives ratings: delivery_rating falls ~0.075 per minute of delay; late (delay > 10 min) orders average roughly 1-1.5 points lower than on-time orders; unhappy customers are also more likely to rate. | [Instructor note] Heavy Rain and Rain days (Mumbai/Kolkata/Pune Jun-Sep, Chennai Oct-Dec) add 6-13 minutes and raise cancellation rates (~3.5% base up to ~8%). | [Instructor note] Lunch (12-13h) and dinner (20-21h) peaks have longer waits; weekends are ~25% busier; order volume rises ~1.3x during IPL months (Mar 22-May 26 2024, Mar 31-May 28 2023). | [Instructor note] Partners in their first ~60 days are ~5 minutes slower; a skill factor per partner creates a spread in partner performance. | [Instructor note] FLAT75 is applied heavily to low-value orders (discount is a large share of order value), making it the worst-ROI promo; WELCOME50 drives new-user orders; IPLFEAST and MONSOON20 only appear in their seasons. | [Instructor note] Restaurant food quality varies independently of delivery speed (food_rating vs delivery_rating can be separated by analysts). | [Instructor note] 8 outlier order_values (100x) distort average order value.

- **salaries** (5259 rows): salary_id:INTEGER, employee_id:INTEGER, effective_date:DATE, annual_ctc:REAL, hike_pct:REAL, change_reason:TEXT
- **attrition** (544 rows): attrition_id:INTEGER, employee_id:INTEGER, exit_date:DATE, exit_type:TEXT, exit_reason:TEXT, notice_period_days:INTEGER, regretted_loss:INTEGER, exit_interview_score:INTEGER
- **performance_reviews** (4786 rows): review_id:INTEGER, employee_id:INTEGER, review_period:TEXT, review_date:DATE, manager_rating:INTEGER, self_rating:INTEGER, goals_met_pct:INTEGER, avg_monthly_overtime_hours:REAL, promotion_recommended:INTEGER
- FKs: employees.department_id->departments.department_id; employees.manager_id->employees.employee_id; salaries.employee_id->employees.employee_id; attrition.employee_id->employees.employee_id; performance_reviews.employee_id->employees.employee_id
- Quality issues: employees: 12 exact duplicate rows (same employee_id twice), so employee_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint; performance_reviews: 10 exact duplicate rows. | employees.gender: ~6% of rows use 'M'/'F' instead of 'Male'/'Female'. | employees.city: ~9% have inconsistent casing/whitespace ('pune', ' Pune'), ~2% NULL; employees.email ~4% NULL. | employees.manager_id is NULL for top-level managers (~5% of employees). | salaries.annual_ctc: 5 rows are 100x outliers (e.g. 120,000,000 instead of 1,200,000). | salaries.hike_pct is NULL for opening-balance and joining rows (about 45% of salary rows). | attrition.exit_interview_score is NULL for ~30% of exits. | CSV only - employees.hire_date and employees.date_of_birth: ~20% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY. | CSV only - salaries.annual_ctc: ~30% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping (e.g. '₹12,50,000'). | CSV only - performance_reviews.review_date: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY.
- Signals (instructor notes): [Instructor note] Attrition is driven by (a) low manager ratings, (b) high average overtime (> ~10 h/month), and (c) low appraisal hikes (< ~4%); employees with all three leave at several times the base rate. | [Instructor note] Customer Support, Sales and Operations have the highest attrition; Finance and HR the lowest; employees with < 2 years tenure leave more. | [Instructor note] Exits spike in April-June (post-appraisal) and Nov-Jan (post-bonus). | [Instructor note] Hike % tracks performance (about +3 points per rating step) while Sales gets ~1 point lower hikes. | [Instructor note] Customer Support has the lowest CTC but the highest overtime; Engineering and Product pay ~25-30% more than average. | [Instructor note] Overtime-heavy exits cite 'Work-life balance / overtime' far more often in exit_reason. | [Instructor note] 5 salary outliers (100x) distort average CTC unless excluded.

## fintech

- **users** (4010 rows): user_id:INTEGER, full_name:TEXT, phone:TEXT, city:TEXT, state:TEXT, age_group:TEXT, kyc_status:TEXT, primary_bank:TEXT, preferred_app:TEXT, upi_id:TEXT, signup_date:DATE
- **merchants** (400 rows): merchant_id:INTEGER, merchant_name:TEXT, category:TEXT, city:TEXT, onboarding_date:DATE, is_verified:INTEGER, mcc_code:INTEGER
- **transactions** (22088 rows): txn_id:INTEGER, user_id:INTEGER, merchant_id:INTEGER, receiver_user_id:INTEGER, txn_type:TEXT, txn_datetime:DATETIME, amount:REAL, payment_app:TEXT, bank:TEXT, device_os:TEXT, status:TEXT, is_flagged:INTEGER
- **failed_transactions** (633 rows): failed_txn_id:INTEGER, txn_id:INTEGER, failure_code:TEXT, failure_reason:TEXT, failed_at:DATETIME, retried:INTEGER, retry_succeeded:INTEGER
- FKs: transactions.user_id->users.user_id; transactions.merchant_id->merchants.merchant_id; transactions.receiver_user_id->users.user_id; failed_transactions.txn_id->transactions.txn_id
- Quality issues: transactions: ~0.4% (about 90) rows are exact duplicates (same txn_id), so txn_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint; users: 10 exact duplicate rows; failed_transactions: 6 exact duplicates. | transactions.amount: 6 rows are 100x outliers. | transactions.merchant_id is NULL for P2P rows (~24%) and receiver_user_id is NULL for non-P2P rows - by design, not an error. | users.city ~10% inconsistent casing/whitespace and ~3% NULL; users.phone ~2% NULL; users.upi_id ~5% NULL; merchants.city ~8% inconsistent casing. | failed_transactions.retry_succeeded is NULL when retried = 0 (~40% of rows). | CSV only - users.signup_date: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY. | CSV only - transactions.txn_datetime: ~15% DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS; transactions.amount: ~12% text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping. | CSV only - failed_transactions.failed_at: ~20% DD-MM-YYYY.
- Signals (instructor notes): [Instructor note] Kaveri Co-op Bank has a much higher failure rate than other banks, concentrated in peak hours (9-10h and 18-20h) with code BANK_SERVER_TIMEOUT (about 15% at peak vs ~2% elsewhere). | [Instructor note] Two platform-wide UPI outages (2023-11-12 18-22h and 2024-10-31 18-22h, Diwali evenings) push failure rates to ~55%, code UPI_SYSTEM_DOWN. | [Instructor note] Failures are ~35% higher on the 1st-3rd of the month (salary days) and amounts above 50,000 fail 2.5x more (LIMIT_EXCEEDED). | [Instructor note] Volume spikes around Diwali windows and month-end; weekends are ~10% higher; evening 18-20h is the busiest slot. | [Instructor note] Network/timeouts are retried and succeed far more often than insufficient-funds failures. | [Instructor note] Late-night (0-4h) large P2P transfers (> 8,000) are flagged ~45% of the time (the fraud-risk signal). | [Instructor note] Customer activity is heavy-tailed; merchant volume is power-law distributed; Fuel/Travel/Electronics have high ticket sizes.

## subscription

- **users** (5208 rows): user_id:INTEGER, email:TEXT, signup_date:DATE, signup_time:TEXT, city:TEXT, platform:TEXT, acquisition_source:TEXT, age_group:TEXT
- **subscriptions** (3308 rows): subscription_id:INTEGER, user_id:INTEGER, plan:TEXT, billing_cycle:TEXT, price_inr:INTEGER, trial_start_date:DATE, paid_start_date:DATE, end_date:DATE, cancel_date:DATE, status:TEXT, renewal_count:INTEGER
- **events** (36383 rows): event_id:INTEGER, user_id:INTEGER, event_time:DATETIME, event_name:TEXT, plan:TEXT, platform:TEXT
- FKs: subscriptions.user_id->users.user_id; events.user_id->users.user_id
- Quality issues: events: ~0.5% (about 100) exact duplicate rows (same event_id); users: 8 exact duplicates. Neither table has a PRIMARY KEY constraint on its id. | events.event_name: ~1.2% of values are UPPERCASE ('APP_OPEN'); events.platform: ~2% are lowercase ('android') - breaks naive GROUP BY. | users.email ~6% NULL; users.city ~4% NULL and ~10% inconsistent casing/whitespace. | events.plan is NULL for events before a plan is chosen (signup and most early engagement events); subscriptions.paid_start_date NULL for users who never paid; cancel_date/end_date NULL by design for active users. | CSV only - users.signup_date ~15% and subscriptions.trial_start_date ~10%: DD-MM-YYYY; events.event_time ~10%: DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS. | CSV only - subscriptions.price_inr: ~40% of rows are text such as '₹299'.
- Signals (instructor notes): [Instructor note] Funnel: signup -> trial_start (~63%) -> payment_success (~36% of trials) -> renewals; iOS converts trials noticeably better (~50%) than Android (~34%). | [Instructor note] The March 2024 signup cohort churns far faster (about 2.7x hazard) - month-1 and month-2 retention is visibly worse than neighbouring cohorts. | [Instructor note] Influencer-sourced users start trials often but convert at less than half the normal rate and churn faster; Referral users convert ~25% better. | [Instructor note] Basic plan churns more than Premium; annual plans have almost no churn in the first year but low renewal at month 12. | [Instructor note] Oct-Nov (Diwali) cohorts convert ~20% better; signups grow strongly through 2024. | [Instructor note] About 3.5% of renewal charges fail (payment_failed), and ~45% of those lead to involuntary cancellation. | [Instructor note] Engagement events (app_open, content_view) cluster in the first 14 days after signup and decay for churners.

## marketing

- **ad_spend** (2109 rows): ad_spend_id:INTEGER, campaign_id:INTEGER, spend_date:DATE, device:TEXT, impressions:INTEGER, clicks:INTEGER, spend_inr:REAL
- **clicks** (21514 rows): click_id:INTEGER, campaign_id:INTEGER, click_time:DATETIME, visitor_id:INTEGER, device:TEXT, city:TEXT, city_tier:TEXT, landing_page:TEXT, cost_inr:REAL
- **conversions** (807 rows): conversion_id:INTEGER, click_id:INTEGER, campaign_id:INTEGER, conversion_time:DATETIME, conversion_type:TEXT, revenue_inr:REAL
- **ab_test_results** (12030 rows): ab_id:INTEGER, user_id:INTEGER, test_name:TEXT, variant:TEXT, assigned_at:DATETIME, device_type:TEXT, city_tier:TEXT, converted:INTEGER, revenue_inr:REAL
- FKs: ad_spend.campaign_id->campaigns.campaign_id; clicks.campaign_id->campaigns.campaign_id; conversions.click_id->clicks.click_id; conversions.campaign_id->campaigns.campaign_id
- Quality issues: clicks: 30 exact duplicate rows (same click_id); ad_spend: 6 exact duplicates; ab_test_results: 20 exact duplicate rows - so these ids carry no PRIMARY KEY constraint. | ab_test_results: 10 users appear in both variants (contaminated assignment) - should be removed before analysis. | ad_spend.spend_inr: 3 rows are 100x outliers. | clicks.city: ~3% NULL and ~7% inconsistent casing/whitespace; clicks.device: ~2% casing issues ('mobile', 'DESKTOP'). | conversions.revenue_inr is NULL for Signup and Lead conversions (~10%) by design. | ab_test_results has no foreign key; it is independent of the campaign tables. | CSV only - campaigns.start_date ~15% DD-MM-YYYY; campaigns.budget_inr ~30% text like '₹12,50,000'. | CSV only - ad_spend.spend_inr ~10% text with rupee symbol; clicks.click_time ~12% DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS; conversions.revenue_inr ~25% text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping.
- Signals (instructor notes): [Instructor note] Campaign 'Influencer Mega Reach Oct-24' burns the largest budget at ~2.3x normal CPC with a conversion rate ~1/8 of a normal influencer campaign - by far the worst ROAS/CAC among revenue-driving campaigns (ROAS about 0.07 vs 5-8 for Search). | [Instructor note] Email and WhatsApp have the lowest CPC and the highest conversion rate (best ROAS); Google Search is the best large-scale paid channel. | [Instructor note] Diwali windows (Oct 25-Nov 14 2023, Oct 20-Nov 3 2024) lift conversion rate by ~25%; Search/Meta Diwali campaigns are the top revenue campaigns. | [Instructor note] Awareness-objective campaigns (YouTube, Display) convert to Signup/Lead mostly and look weak on last-click revenue. | [Instructor note] Desktop converts ~35% better than mobile; Metro converts better than Tier-2. | [Instructor note] A/B test: treatment lifts conversion from ~9.5% to ~11% overall (about +1.5pp, p roughly 0.01-0.03), driven by Mobile (about +1.8pp) while Desktop shows an insignificant +0.3pp; treatment AOV is ~4% lower (free shipping cost), so revenue per user lift is smaller than conversion lift. | [Instructor note] Contaminated users, duplicates and 100x spend outliers must be cleaned before computing cost metrics or test statistics.

## retail

- **stores** (24 rows): store_id:INTEGER, store_code:TEXT, store_name:TEXT, city:TEXT, state:TEXT, region:TEXT, store_format:TEXT, opened_on:DATE, carpet_area_sqft:INTEGER
- **sales** (24350 rows): sale_id:INTEGER, sale_datetime:DATETIME, store_id:INTEGER, sku_id:TEXT, category:TEXT, quantity:INTEGER, unit_price_inr:REAL, discount_pct:REAL, net_amount_inr:REAL, payment_mode:TEXT
- **inventory** (13824 rows): inventory_id:INTEGER, snapshot_date:DATE, store_id:INTEGER, sku_id:TEXT, category:TEXT, stock_on_hand:INTEGER, reorder_level:INTEGER, units_sold_in_month:INTEGER, days_out_of_stock:INTEGER
- **targets** (504 rows): target_id:INTEGER, store_id:INTEGER, target_month:TEXT, target_net_sales_inr:REAL, target_units:INTEGER
- FKs: sales.store_id->stores.store_id; inventory.store_id->stores.store_id; targets.store_id->stores.store_id
- Quality issues: sales: 350 exact duplicate rows (same sale_id twice), so sale_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint. | sales.discount_pct: NULL for ~4% of rows; net_amount_inr already reflects the discount, so it is still populated. | sales.payment_mode: ~8% inconsistent casing/whitespace ('upi', ' Card'), ~1% NULL. | sales.net_amount_inr: 6 rows are 100x outliers. | stores.city: ~8% casing/whitespace issues. | inventory.stock_on_hand: ~1% NULL. | targets.target_net_sales_inr: ~3% NULL; no targets exist for the East region stores. | CSV only - sales.sale_datetime: ~15% of rows use DD-MM-YYYY; sales.net_amount_inr: ~25% are rupee text with Indian grouping. | CSV only - inventory.snapshot_date: ~12% of rows use DD-MM-YYYY; targets.target_net_sales_inr: ~15% are rupee text. | No product master table: sku_id and category are denormalised codes.
- Signals (instructor notes): [Instructor note] Stockouts: Velachery (Chennai), Adajan (Surat), Gomti Nagar (Lucknow) and Kharadi (Pune) stores have frequent stockouts (days_out_of_stock > 0 for many SKUs) and roughly 30% lower sales volume than peers. | [Instructor note] Diwali (Oct-Nov) and the 2024 Navratri window spike sales; Republic Day and Independence Day sale weeks give smaller spikes. | [Instructor note] Home Decor is slow-moving: about 5% of sales volume, but stock covers 6-10 months of demand, so it is overstocked. | [Instructor note] East region stores (Kolkata, Patna, Guwahati) have no targets, so target attainment can only be compared for the other regions. | [Instructor note] Targets are set at 90-115% of actual sales, so attainment clusters near 100% with a few misses. | [Instructor note] 2024 prices are about 6% higher than 2023 for every SKU, so compare volume and value separately. | [Instructor note] Sales are a sampled extract of about one transaction line per store per day, so use rates and shares rather than absolute totals. | [Instructor note] 6 net_amount outliers (100x) distort totals unless excluded.
